# jsonstor-elasticsearch

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### Documents are stored on an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. Documents are stored on an Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server.

***It carries no database driver.*** The server is reached over HTTP with the runtime's
  own `fetch`, so this package adds nothing to a project beyond `jsonstor` and `jsongin`.

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-elasticsearch
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-elasticsearch' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-elasticsearch', {
	Server: '...',
	Port: 9200,
	Encrypt: false,
	IndexName: '...',
	PrimaryKey: "_id",
	PrimaryKeyMutable: false,
	PayloadField: "jsonstor_document",
	Mappings: [],
	UserName: "",
	Password: "",
} );
```

Versions
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This package answers to more than one name. Pass any of these to `GetStorage()`;
  a name which is not listed is refused.

| Name | Dialect it uses | Measured against |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | its own | 1.3 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | its own | 7.17 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v8` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v8.19` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | 8.19 |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v9` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | - |
| `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v9.5` | `jsonstor-elasticsearch-v7.17` | 9.5 |
| `jsonstor-opensearch` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v1` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v2` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v2.19` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | 2.19 |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v3` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | - |
| `jsonstor-opensearch-v3.8` | `jsonstor-opensearch-v1.3` | 3.8 |

A name with its own dialect was measured against that server version and covers every
  later one up to the next such name. The rest resolve to one of those. The bare name
  follows the newest dialect this package carries, which is what most callers want.

A name whose dialect your server cannot serve is refused on the first operation, naming
  the version you asked for and the one the server needs.

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `Server` | ***Yes*** | - | The name or address of the Elasticsearch or OpenSearch server. |
| `Port` | No | `9200` | The service port of the server. |
| `Encrypt` | No | `false` | Reach the server over `https` rather than `http`. There is no `TrustServerCertificate` beside it, because this adapter has no driver except the global `fetch`, which offers no supported way to relax certificate verification. |
| `IndexName` | ***Yes*** | - | The index this storage reads and writes. It is the collection: one index holds one collection's documents. |
| `PrimaryKey` | No | `"_id"` | The document field which is the identifier. Its value becomes the Elasticsearch `_id`. `IdField` is the former spelling and still works. |
| `PrimaryKeyMutable` | No | `false` | Allow an update or a replacement to change the identifier. Off by default, so an operation which would move it is refused by name rather than silently discarded. |
| `PayloadField` | No | `"jsonstor_document"` | The field which stores the document. It cannot be empty: Elasticsearch reserves `_id` as a metadata field, so a document carrying this family's default identifier field cannot be stored at the top level. See the notes. |
| `Mappings` | No | `[]` | The payload fields to give an explicit mapping, as `{ Name, Type }` and optionally `NullValue`. Only a mapped field can be searched on the server; everything else is stored, returned, and filtered by `jsongin`. See the notes. |
| `UserName` | No | `""` | The user to connect as. Empty means none, which is what a server with security disabled expects. |
| `Password` | No | `""` | That user's password. Empty means none. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***One package, two products.*** Elasticsearch and OpenSearch speak the same Query DSL over the same REST surface, and six servers - Elasticsearch 7.17, 8.19 and 9.5, OpenSearch 1.3, 2.19 and 3.8 - answered every one of jsongin's thirty one query operators identically. ***Elasticsearch 6.8 is below the floor***: it refuses the `case_insensitive` parameter on a `regexp` query, which arrived in 7.10, and it has mapping types where 7.x does not.
- ***This adapter installs no database driver, and that is a measurement rather than a preference.*** `@elastic/elasticsearch` refuses an OpenSearch server twice over - a documented product check, and then a vendor media type OpenSearch answers `406` to - so no single client library reaches both products dependably. The runtime's own `fetch` reaches both, which is where the `>=18.0.0` engine floor comes from.
- ***An Elasticsearch index is a jsonstor collection.*** `IndexName` names it, and one index holds one collection. `DropStorage` is a single `DELETE` which removes exactly this storage's documents.
- ***The document travels in a payload, and it has to.*** Elasticsearch reserves `_id` as a metadata field and refuses a document body containing one - which is exactly what this family's default identifier field is called. So the Elasticsearch `_id` holds `String( )` of the identifier and the document itself lives in `PayloadField`, where it keeps its own types. Unlike `jsonstor-couchdb`, there is no second configuration: `PayloadField` cannot be empty.
- ***What comes back is exactly what went in, even where the search index disagrees with it.*** Elasticsearch coerces values on the way into its index and leaves the stored document alone: a field mapped `double` which receives the string `"10"` is *indexed* as `10` and *returned* as `"10"`. So an absent field stays apart from one holding null, a number does not come back a string, and an object keeps its field order - while a search on that field may match more documents than the criteria does. ***That is why the answer is always re-checked by `jsongin`.***
- ***Only a field named in `Mappings` can be searched on the server.*** The payload is mapped `dynamic: false`, so an undeclared field is stored and returned but never indexed - and a criteria about it is decided by `jsongin` instead. This is the same model the SQL adapters use for their columns - the setting is named for Elasticsearch's own word rather than theirs, because a mapping is not a column - and it means a storage with no `Mappings` is correct and simply does no pushdown.
  - ***`Type` is an Elasticsearch field type*** - `keyword`, `text`, `long`, `integer`, `short`, `byte`, `double`, `float`, `boolean` or `date`.
  - ***A `text` field is never searched on the server.*** An analyzed field answers the same for `widget` and `Widget`, which is the analyzer working correctly and the wrong answer for an equality. Declare one to get full-text search of your own; this adapter will not push a criteria into it.
  - ***`NullValue` is the only way `$exists` can be answered by the server.*** Elasticsearch does not index a null, so without a sentinel a field holding null is indistinguishable from one that is absent.
- ***A criteria is pushed down to the Query DSL, and what it cannot read is decided by `jsongin`.*** `$and`, `$or`, `$exists`, `$regex`, `$all`, `$elemMatch`, the comparisons, `$in` and the plain `{ field: value }` form all narrow the search; the negations, `$mod`, the bitwise operators, `$size`, `$type`, `$expr` and jsongin's own extensions are decided by `jsongin`. ***The answer is the same one either way*** - what a dropped operator costs is a document read, never a wrong result.
- ***A negation is never pushed down, and the reason is the coercion above.*** A search which admits extra documents is safe; negating one would *reject* documents the criteria admits, which is the one error a pushdown may not make. So a negation is left to `jsongin` entirely.
- ***Every write refreshes the index.*** Elasticsearch is near real time by default - a document becomes searchable about a second after it is written - and this adapter asks for a refresh on every write so that a read which follows a write sees it, the way every other adapter in this family behaves.
- ***A collection reads back in the order it was written.*** Insertion order is recorded in a field of its own, and that field is never part of a document. Use `FindMany2` with a `Sort` when you need a different order.
- ***A read pages with `search_after` rather than `from` and `size`.*** Paging by offset stops at ten thousand documents on a default index, and raising that limit would be this adapter reconfiguring a server it did not create.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage-Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).
